questions.question: A shopkeeper marked an article at ₹5,000. The shopkeeper allows successive discounts of 20%, 15% and 10%. The selling price of the article is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given percentage discounts into multiplying fractions: 20% = 4/5, 15% = 17/20, 10% = 9/10.

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (Fraction 1) × (Fraction 2) × (Fraction 3)

SP = 5000 × 4/5 × 17/20 × 9/10

SP = 5000 × 612/1000 = 3060

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,060.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹5,000

Successive discounts = 20%, 15% and 10%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d904b7c1afec448f5252dd375de5a2d2ce01f58e3a57d9310f4edb027e7cd41c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100) × (1 − D₃/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 5000 × (1 − 20/100) × (1 − 15/100) × (1 − 10/100)

⇒ SP = 5000 × (80/100) × (85/100) × (90/100)

⇒ SP = 5000 × (4/5) × (17/20) × (9/10)

⇒ SP = 5000 × (612/1000)

⇒ SP = 5 × 612

⇒ SP = 3060

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,060.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Single Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by (a + b − a×b/100)%.

Marked Price and Cost Price Relationship

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly calculated using: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer pretends to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percentage is found using: Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100%.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs 1,000 After two successive discounts, it is sold for Rs 600, If the first discount is x% and the second discount is 25%, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the article = Rs.1000 

Selling Price (SP) of the article = Rs.600

First discount = x% 

Second discount = 25%

**Formula used:**

Discount = MP - SP 

SP after discount = MP × (100 - Discount%)/100

**Calculation:**

SP of the article after the first discount = 1000 × (100 - x)/100 = 10 × (100 - x) 

SP of the article after the second discount = 10 × (100 - x) × (100 - 25)/100 

⇒ 10 × (100 - x) × 75/100 = 600 

⇒ (100 - x) = 600 × 100/75 × 1/10 

⇒ 100 - x = 80 

⇒ x = 20

**∴ The first discount percent = 20%**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Formulas used:

Discount rate = Discount/MP × 100 

Also, x + y -xy/100 

Second discount = 25%

Total Discount = 1000 - 600 = 400 

Effective rate of discount = 400/1000 × 100 

⇒ 40% 

Effective rate of discount = x + y - xy/100 

⇒ x + 25% - x × 25/100 

⇒ 40% = x + 25% - x/4 

⇒ 15% = x - x/4 

⇒ 15% = 3x/4 

**⇒ x = 15% × 4/3 = 20%**

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 40% and 30% are equal to a single discount of:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is given by the direct formula:

Equivalent Discount = [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = [40 + 30 − (40 × 30) ÷ 100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = [70 − 1200 ÷ 100]%

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 70 − 12 = 58%

**∴ The correct answer is 58%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two successive discounts = 40% and 30%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b9321f77262e2d25da32f58c871bc9476373d8d9ed868b83dd4eb258d0b83d8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) of the article be 100.

⇒ Price after the first discount of 40% = 100 − (40% of 100) = 100 − 40 = 60

⇒ Price after the second discount of 30% = 60 − (30% of 60) = 60 − 18 = 42

⇒ The final Selling Price (SP) becomes 42.

⇒ Total Discount given = Original MP − Final SP

⇒ Total Discount = 100 − 42 = 58

⇒ Since the base MP is 100, the equivalent discount percentage is exactly 58%.

**∴ The correct answer is 58%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount for Three Items

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, the final selling price is calculated as: SP = MP × (1 − a ÷ 100) × (1 − b ÷ 100) × (1 − c ÷ 100).

Marked Price and Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the item. Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount.

Single vs Successive Discounts

A single flat discount of (x + y)% will always result in a lower selling price (i.e., a better deal for the buyer) compared to two successive discounts of x% and y% applied one after the other on the same article.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 30% more than the cost price. A discount of 15% is offered on the marked price. By what percentage is the final price more than the cost price?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Marked price = 30% more than Cost price

Discount = 15%

**FORMULA USED:**

Discount % = (Discount / M.P.) × 100 

Discount = M.P. - S.P. 

Where, M.P. = Marked price, S.P. = Selling price.

**CALCULATION:**

Let's assume the Cost price will be Rs100.

According to the question,

M.P. = 30% more than the cost price.

⇒ M.P. = ( 100 + 100 × 30/100 ) = Rs.130.

Now, discount% = 15

⇒ Discount% =( Discount /M.P.) × 100

⇒ 15 = ( Discount / 130) × 100

⇒ Discount = Rs.19.5

Now, S.P. = ( M.P. - Discount ) = ( 130 - 19.5 ) = Rs.110.5.

Now, S.P. = final price = Rs110.5 and Cost price = Rs.100

Difference = ( 110.5 -100) = 10.5 

Required percentage =( 10.5 / 100 ) × 100 = 10.5%.

**Hence, the final price is 10.5% more than the Cost price.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Concept used:

⇒ 10/13 = (100 - 15%)/(100 + x%)

⇒ 10/13 = 85/(100 + x%)

⇒ (100 + x%) = (85 × 13)/10

⇒ (100 + x%) = 110.5

⇒ x% = (110.5 - 100) = 10.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 10.5%.**

questions.question: The marked price of an item is 25% more than that of its cost price. If a discount of 10% is given on the marked price, then the gain percentage is:
An article is sold for Rs. 560 after two successive discounts of 30% and 20%. What is marked price of the article?
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling price of the article after two successive discounts = Rs. 560

First discount: 30%

Second discount: 20%

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Marked price - (Discount 1% × Marked price) - (Discount 2% × Marked price)

**Calculation:**

Let's solve the question:

Let the marked price of the article be "M".

Selling price after the first discount = M - (30/100)M = (70/100)M = 0.7M

Selling price after the second discount = 0.7M - (20/100)(0.7M) = (0.7M) - (0.14M) = 0.56M

Given that the selling price after the two discounts is Rs. 560, we can set up the equation:

0.56M = 560

To find the marked price (M), divide both sides of the equation by 0.56:

M = 560/0.56

questions.question: Ramlal marks up his goods by 40% and gives a discount of 10%. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For successive percentage changes, use the net effect formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +40% and Discount (b) = −10%

Net Profit % = 40 − 10 + [40 × (−10)] ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 30 − 4 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 40%

Discount Percentage = 10%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/648b541e29f9eb1e8917f94774372ff3c9a49a15fd6e46c915a4c6afa9608b03.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + (40% of 100) = 140

⇒ Discount given = 10% on MP = (10 ÷ 100) × 140 = 14

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 140 − 14 = 126

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 126 − 100 = 26

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (26 ÷ 100) × 100 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is always calculated by applying the markup percentage on the Cost Price (CP). Formula: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is given by the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP to MP Ratio

The direct relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by the ratio: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: Find a single discount percentage equivalent to successive discounts of 10%, 20% and 25%.

Effective discount = d₁ + d₂ - d₁ × d₂ over 100

Final discount = 28 + 25 - 25 × 28over 100 = 53 - 7 = 46
